title: Three-round trivial-schedule IEM full-XRKA query frontier
summary: Close the unknown two-query-budget region between the proved security bound and the generic attack on three-round IEM with one repeated key.

formal_statement.body: For $\operatorname{EM}[n,3,I]$ with three independent public random permutations and the same uniformly random $n$-bit key at every key addition, determine the adaptive bidirectional XOR-related-key security frontier throughout the gap between $\operatorname{Adv}\le 6q_e q_p/2^n+4q_e^2/2^n$ and the generic attack boundary $q_e q_p\approx 2^n$, by giving matching security and attack bounds.

scope.domain: Three-round iterated Even--Mansour with a trivial key schedule under adaptive bidirectional XOR-related-key attacks.
assumptions: One uniformly random $n$-bit master key is reused in all round-key additions.
The three public random permutations are independent.
Both construction and primitive access are adaptive and bidirectional.
scope.unresolved_remainder: The complete Figure 4 region between the source theorem and the generic $q_e q_p\approx2^n$ attack remains without matching bounds.

progress.summary: The source identifies the remaining query-complexity region for three-round trivial-schedule IEM in its Figure 4.
